answer: Juniper-Ring Routing Distance. Agents route work only to peers reachable through disjoint neighbor paths; each new identity must be embedded by existing agents whose edges are scarce and locally recorded, so clones cluster on few paths. The rule scores an identity by count of distinct inbound paths from established neighborhoods, and drops work below three. Attacker pays per identity in real edge slots and routing delay, not tokens. Quill logs expose duplicate path signatures. Yarrow scoring thresholds tighten as path reuse rises, forcing costly topology reconstruction per clone.
